questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 284 · Chapter 1 · Air Force traditions · Source pages 16–19 · Objective(s) 15–19)

questions.q: Which statement best defines Serve faithfully?
options: doing what is right even when no one is watching
cadet airmen, cadet NCOs, company-grade cadet officers, and field-grade cadet officers
CAP’s basic moral guideposts: Integrity, Volunteer Service, Excellence, and Respect
be true to the Cadet Program and do what you promised
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 285 · Chapter 1 · Cadet Oath · Source pages 14–15 · Objective(s) 14)

questions.q: Which statement best defines Communication?
options: the body’s response to change, which can energize or harm depending on level and management
anything that causes a stress response
the process of sharing meaning through sending, receiving, and responding to messages
being willing to listen, work, accept feedback, and take responsibility for growth
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 286 · Chapter 2 · Communication · Source pages 51–56 · Objective(s) 41–47)

questions.q: Which situation is the best example of Integrity First?
options: A cadet follows through on CAP commitments consistently
A cadet reports an accidental equipment break instead of hiding it
A cadet keeps working toward a long-term goal without lying, cheating, or stealing
An experienced cadet stays late to help a new cadet learn drill
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 287 · Chapter 1 · Core Values · Source pages 10 · Objective(s) 6–7)

questions.q: Which situation is the best example of Self-discipline?
options: A squadron issue normally moves upward one level at a time
A cadet resists checking a phone until dashboardwork is finished
A cadet bypasses the flight staff and emails the national commander about a routine issue
A cadet treats the Cadet Oath as a real commitment, not just words to memorize
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 288 · Chapter 1 · Personal leadership · Source pages 11–12 · Objective(s) 9)

questions.q: Which situation is the best example of Serve faithfully?
options: A junior walks on the senior person’s left
A cadet first takes a routine issue to the element leader or immediate supervisor
A cadet follows through on CAP commitments consistently
A cadet follows a safety instruction but refuses an obviously immoral order
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 289 · Chapter 1 · Cadet Oath · Source pages 14–15 · Objective(s) 14)

questions.q: A cadet says, “Obey every demand even when it is unsafe or immoral” Which response best corrects that misunderstanding?
options: follow lawful and moral guidance from more experienced leaders
A list used only during inspections
Marching whose only purpose is entertainment
Obey every demand even when it is unsafe or immoral
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 290 · Chapter 1 · Cadet Oath · Source pages 15 · Objective(s) 14)

questions.q: Which situation is the best example of Drill and ceremonies?
options: A cadet studies weak areas, practices, and asks for feedback
A cadet bypasses the flight staff and emails the national commander about a routine issue
A cadet notices weak math skills and schedules extra study time
A flight improves unity by practicing commands together
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 291 · Chapter 1 · Drill · Source pages 22–23 · Objective(s) 24–25)

questions.q: A cadet says, “Doing whatever protects your own reputation” Which response best corrects that misunderstanding?
options: Doing whatever protects your own reputation
doing what is right even when no one is watching
Thinking only about how others need to improve
A leader receives authority but cannot be questioned
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 292 · Chapter 1 · Core Values · Source pages 10 · Objective(s) 6–7)

questions.q: Which statement best defines Clear conscience?
options: freedom from shame that comes from keeping promises and doing right
answering for your actions and accepting the consequences of your choices
be true to the Cadet Program and do what you promised
the pattern of moral choices and habits that shows who a person really is
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 293 · Chapter 1 · Warrior spirit · Source pages 8 · Objective(s) 4)

questions.q: Which statement best defines Customs and courtesies?
options: a solemn public promise that places personal honor and reputation on the line
small but important expressions of politeness and mutual respect
the principle that the power to direct others must be matched by accountability for results
the trust and respect earned through repeated honorable conduct
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 294 · Chapter 1 · Air Force traditions · Source pages 16–19 · Objective(s) 15–19)

questions.q: Which statement best defines Respect?
options: directing thoughts, emotions, and actions toward a meaningful purpose
be true to the Cadet Program and do what you promised
defending human dignity and treating people with fairness, politeness, and tolerance
answering for your actions and accepting the consequences of your choices
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 295 · Chapter 1 · Core Values · Source pages 10 · Objective(s) 6–7)

questions.q: Which statement best defines Drill and ceremonies?
options: the trust and respect earned through repeated honorable conduct
the pattern of moral choices and habits that shows who a person really is
precision movement that develops teamwork, self-discipline, attention to detail, and excellence
the right-hand position traditionally given to the senior person
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 296 · Chapter 1 · Drill · Source pages 22–23 · Objective(s) 24–25)

questions.q: Which statement best defines Uniform privilege?
options: the formal procedure of approaching, saluting, reporting, conducting business, and departing
honestly monitoring and judging your own strengths, weaknesses, and actions
defending human dignity and treating people with fairness, politeness, and tolerance
the idea that wearing an Air Force-style uniform carries a special duty to wear it correctly
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 297 · Chapter 1 · Uniform · Source pages 20 · Objective(s) 22)

questions.q: A cadet says, “Clothing that matters only for photographs” Which response best corrects that misunderstanding?
options: A list used only during inspections
Clothing that matters only for photographs
a means of learning self-discipline, responsibility, self-respect, accuracy, and attention to detail
Agreeing with every idea regardless of merit
questions.explanation: Official CAP Learn to Lead preparation question. (Question 298 · Chapter 1 · Uniform · Source pages 20–21 · Objective(s) 20–22)

options: Only physical attractiveness
cadet airmen, cadet NCOs, company-grade cadet officers, and field-grade cadet officers
All cadet grades belong to one category
Popularity automatically proves good character

CAP’s basic moral guideposts: Integrity, Volunteer Service, Excellence, and Respect

Actions that prove one person is less valuable than another

CAP_DRILL.description: Master Civil Air Patrol drill movements, commands, and ceremonial procedures under CAPP 60-33. Access the official drill pamphlet here: https://www.gocivilairpatrol.com/media/cms/P060_033_2_AUG_2016_42436A7A93EE9.pdf

questions.q: Which official publication governs Civil Air Patrol Drill & Ceremonies?
options: CAPR 52-16
CAPP 60-33
CAPR 39-1
DAFPAM 34-1203
questions.explanation: CAPP 60-33 is the official Civil Air Patrol Drill and Ceremonies Pamphlet.

questions.q: In CAP drill, what is the standard Quick Time cadence rate?
options: 90 to 100 steps/min
110 to 130 steps/min
100 to 120 steps/min
180 steps/min
questions.explanation: CAPP 60-33 specifies Quick Time cadence as 100 to 120 steps per minute.

questions.q: On which foot is the command 'TO THE REAR, MARCH' given in CAP drill?
options: Left foot
Right foot
Either foot
Both feet
questions.explanation: The command 'TO THE REAR, MARCH' is given as the right foot strikes the ground.

questions.q: What is the standard step length for Quick Time in CAP drill?
options: 15 inches
18 inches
24 inches
30 inches
questions.explanation: Standard Quick Time step length in CAP drill is 24 inches.

questions.q: At the Position of Attention, what angle should your feet form?
options: 45 degrees
60 degrees
30 degrees
90 degrees
questions.explanation: At Position of Attention, feet form a 45-degree angle.

questions.q: What is the step length for Half Step in CAP marching?
options: 6 inches
12 inches
15 inches
18 inches
questions.explanation: Half Step length is 12 inches.

questions.q: In CAP ceremonies, on which foot is 'EYES, RIGHT' called?
options: Left foot
Either foot
Standing position
Right foot
questions.explanation: Eyes Right is given on the right foot.

questions.q: What is the standard distance between ranks in a CAP flight formation?
options: 30 inches
40 inches
60 inches
24 inches
questions.explanation: Distance between ranks in a flight is 40 inches.

questions.q: How is Normal Interval measured between cadets in a rank?
options: Left arm extended horizontally
Right arm extended horizontally
Left hand on hip
Right hand on hip
questions.explanation: Normal interval is measured by extending the left arm horizontally at shoulder height.

questions.q: How is Close Interval measured during alignment?
options: Right hand on hip
Elbows touching
Left hand on hip
12-inch gap
questions.explanation: Close interval is measured by placing the left hand on the hip.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a Preparatory Command?
options: When to move
What movement to execute
Who executes the movement
How fast to step
questions.explanation: The preparatory command tells formation members what movement is to be executed.

questions.q: What does the Command of Execution specify?
options: When to execute the movement
The direction of movement
The cadence rate
Which foot to start on
questions.explanation: The command of execution indicates when the movement is to be performed.

questions.q: Which command revokes an incorrect preparatory command?
options: FALL OUT
REST
DISMISSED
AS YOU WERE
questions.explanation: 'As You Were' revokes an improper preparatory command.

questions.q: What is the cadence rate for Double Time in CAP drill?
options: 120 steps/min
180 steps/min
150 steps/min
200 steps/min
questions.explanation: Double Time cadence is 180 steps per minute.

questions.q: What is the length of a Double Time step?
options: 18 inches
24 inches
30 inches
36 inches
questions.explanation: Step length for Double Time is 30 inches.

questions.q: On which foot is 'Right Flank, MARCH' given while marching?
options: Right foot
Left foot
Either foot
Standing position
questions.explanation: 'Right Flank, MARCH' is called as the right foot strikes the ground.

questions.q: On which foot is 'Left Flank, MARCH' given while marching?
options: Right foot
Left foot
Either foot
Both feet
questions.explanation: 'Left Flank, MARCH' is called as the left foot strikes the ground.

questions.q: At Parade Rest, how far apart are feet positioned?
options: 6 inches
10 inches
12 inches
18 inches
questions.explanation: At PARADE, REST, feet are moved 12 inches apart measured from the inside of heels.

questions.q: What is allowed at the position of AT EASE?
options: Right foot may move, must remain silent
May talk quietly
Left foot must remain fixed
May leave formation
questions.explanation: At AT EASE, cadets may move their right foot provided they stay silent.

questions.q: What freedom is granted at the position of REST?
options: May leave the area
Must keep head strictly straight
No movement permitted
May talk quietly with right foot in place
questions.explanation: At REST, cadets may talk and move, keeping their right foot in place.

questions.q: What does the command 'FALL OUT' require formation members to do?
options: Dismissed completely
Leave formation but stay in immediate area
Turn 180 degrees
Sit down immediately
questions.explanation: 'FALL OUT' allows cadets to leave their position in formation but remain nearby.

questions.q: What does the command 'DISMISSED' signify?
options: Terminates the drill period
Re-forms the flight
Marches flight off area
Puts flight at ease
questions.explanation: 'DISMISSED' terminates the duty or drill instruction period.

questions.q: What is the primary role of a Guidon Bearer in ceremonies?
options: Flies air target drones
Leads physical training
Carries the unit flag/emblem standard
Inspects uniforms
questions.explanation: A guidon bearer carries the organizational colors/flag.

questions.q: In Column Formation, who serves as the base when performing Column Right?
options: First element leader
Third element leader
Flight commander
Flight guide
questions.explanation: In a column of threes, the element leader of the third element is the base.

questions.q: On which foot is 'Column Right, MARCH' given?
options: Right foot
Left foot
Either foot
Heels together
questions.explanation: 'Column Right, MARCH' is called on the right foot.

questions.q: On which foot is 'Column Left, MARCH' given?
options: Right foot
Left foot
Either foot
Standing position
questions.explanation: 'Column Left, MARCH' is called on the left foot.

questions.q: What is the cadence rate during 'Mark Time, MARCH'?
options: 60 steps/min
180 steps/min
80 steps/min
100 to 120 steps/min
questions.explanation: Mark Time cadence remains identical to Quick Time (100-120 bpm).

questions.q: How high are feet raised during Mark Time?
options: 2 inches
6 inches
4 inches
12 inches
questions.explanation: In Mark Time, feet are raised 4 inches off the ground.

questions.q: On which foot is the command 'Flight, HALT' given while marching in Quick Time?
options: Either foot
Left foot only
Right foot only
Both feet together
questions.explanation: 'Flight, HALT' can be given on either foot.

questions.q: How many steps are taken after the command of execution for 'HALT'?
options: No additional steps
1 additional step
2 additional steps
3 additional steps
questions.explanation: After 'Flight, HALT', one additional step is taken before halting completely.

questions.q: In a 4-rank flight executing 'Open Ranks, MARCH', how many steps does the 1st rank take?
options: 1 step
2 steps
3 steps
4 steps
questions.explanation: In Open Ranks, the 1st rank takes 3 steps forward.

questions.q: How many steps forward does the 2nd rank take during Open Ranks?
options: 1 step
2 steps
3 steps
Stands fast
questions.explanation: The 2nd rank takes 2 steps forward during Open Ranks.

questions.q: How many steps forward does the 3rd rank take during Open Ranks?
options: 1 step
2 steps
3 steps
Stands fast
questions.explanation: The 3rd rank takes 1 step forward during Open Ranks.

questions.q: What action does the 4th rank take during 'Open Ranks, MARCH'?
options: Takes 1 step backward
Takes 1 step forward
Takes 2 steps backward
Stands fast
questions.explanation: The 4th rank stands fast during Open Ranks.

questions.q: What action completes alignment after 'Dress Right, DRESS'?
options: Returns head and eyes to the front
Executes About Face
Returns arms to sides
Puts flight at ease
questions.explanation: 'Ready, FRONT' brings head and eyes back to the front.

questions.q: On what pivot points is a Right Face executed?
options: Left heel, right ball
Both heels simultaneously
Right heel, left ball
Both balls of feet
questions.explanation: Right Face is executed on the heel of the right foot and ball of left foot.

questions.q: How many degrees does the body turn during a Left Face?
options: 45 degrees
90 degrees
180 degrees
360 degrees
questions.explanation: Left Face turns the body 90 degrees to the left.

questions.q: How many degrees and in what direction is an About Face executed?
options: 90 degrees left
90 degrees right
180 degrees clockwise
180 degrees counter-clockwise
questions.explanation: About Face turns the body 180 degrees clockwise.

questions.q: Where is the right foot placed initially during an About Face?
options: Right toe behind left heel
Left toe behind right heel
Right heel beside left toe
Both feet parallel
questions.explanation: During About Face, the right toe is placed half-foot-length behind left heel.

questions.q: Where are Element Leaders positioned in Line Formation?
options: Extreme left
Extreme right
Center
Behind the rank
questions.explanation: In Line Formation, element leaders are positioned on the extreme right of their element.

questions.q: Where are Element Leaders positioned in a Column Formation?
options: At the rear
To the left side
At the front of each element
In the center rank
questions.explanation: In Column Formation, element leaders lead the front of each column.

questions.q: Where does the Flight Sergeant position when the Flight Commander takes over in line formation?
options: 3 paces centered in rear
3 paces centered in front
6 paces centered in front
1 pace to the right
questions.explanation: Flight Sergeant positioning in line formation is 3 paces centered behind the flight.

questions.q: Where does the Flight Commander stand relative to a flight in Line Formation?
options: 3 paces in front
3 paces in rear
6 paces centered in front
1 pace to the left
questions.explanation: Flight Commander position in line formation is 6 paces centered in front.

questions.q: What degree turn does an 'Incline' command describe?
options: 90-degree turn
Slight direction shift under 45 degrees
Complete 180-degree turn
Oblique 45-degree turn
questions.explanation: 'Incline to the Right' makes a slight directional adjustment under 45 degrees.

questions.q: What degree angle turn is executed for 'Right Oblique, MARCH'?
options: 45 degrees
90 degrees
30 degrees
60 degrees
questions.explanation: 'Right Oblique, MARCH' executes a 45-degree turn.

questions.q: On which foot is 'Right Oblique, MARCH' called?
options: Left foot only
Right foot only
Standing position
Right foot for right oblique, left for left oblique
questions.explanation: 'Oblique, MARCH' is issued on the foot in the direction of turn.

questions.q: Which command resumes forward marching from an Oblique movement?
options: Forward, MARCH
Resume, MARCH
Quick Time, MARCH
As You Were
questions.explanation: 'Resume, MARCH' returns marching from oblique to original line of advance.

questions.q: How many degrees turn of head and eyes is executed during 'EYES, RIGHT'?
options: 30 degrees
90 degrees
45 degrees
60 degrees
questions.explanation: Eyes Right angle is 45 degrees toward the reviewing officer.

questions.q: Who maintains head and eyes straightforward during 'EYES, RIGHT' in pass in review?
options: Right element leader
Flight commander
Guidon bearer
Left element leader
questions.explanation: The element leader on the right side does not turn head or eyes during Eyes Right.

questions.q: At what distance is a hand salute rendered to an oncoming officer?
options: 2 paces away
6 paces away
10 paces away
15 paces away
questions.explanation: Hand salute is rendered when reporting or when officers pass.

questions.q: Where does the tip of the right index finger touch during a proper Hand Salute?
options: Center of forehead
Left eyebrow
Nose bridge
Right eyebrow or corner of glasses frame
questions.explanation: The salute tip of forefinger touches the right eyebrow/glasses frame.

questions.q: What is the standard arm swing distance when marching in Quick Time?
options: 6 inches front, 3 inches rear
12 inches front, 6 inches rear
9 inches front, 4 inches rear
3 inches front, 3 inches rear
questions.explanation: Arm swing during Quick Time marching is 6 inches to front and 3 inches to rear.

questions.q: How are fingers held during Quick Time marching?
options: Fists tightly clenched
Palms flat against legs
Cupped naturally with thumbs along seam lines
Open flat fingers
questions.explanation: Fingers are naturally cupped while marching in Quick Time.

questions.q: How many total counts are called out during 'Count Cadence, COUNT'?
options: 4 counts
8 counts
12 counts
16 counts
questions.explanation: Count Cadence is executed for 8 counts.

questions.q: What is the exact vocalized response to 'Count Cadence, COUNT'?
options: Left, Right, Left, Right
questions.explanation: Cadence counts are 'ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR, ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR'.

questions.q: Which command permits cadets to break cadence and talk while marching?
options: Double Time, MARCH
Half Step, MARCH
At Ease, MARCH
Route Step, MARCH
questions.explanation: 'Route Step, MARCH' allows marching out of cadence.

questions.q: Which command permits breaking cadence but enforces silence while marching?
options: Route Step, MARCH
At Ease, MARCH
Quick Time, MARCH
Mark Time, MARCH
questions.explanation: 'At Ease, MARCH' breaks cadence but requires silence while marching.

questions.q: On which foot is 'Change Step, MARCH' called?
options: Right foot
Either foot
Left foot or right depending on command striking foot
Both feet
questions.explanation: Change Step is executed by stepping up with the toe of the rear foot to the heel of lead foot.

questions.q: Which command returns an opened formation to normal rank distance?
options: Close Ranks, MARCH
Normal Ranks, MARCH
Form Flight, MARCH
Assemble, MARCH
questions.explanation: Close Ranks brings ranks back to 40-inch normal distance.

questions.q: In Close Ranks, what action does the 1st rank take?
options: Takes 3 steps back
Stands fast
Takes 1 step back
Takes 2 steps back
questions.explanation: In 4-rank close ranks, 1st rank stands fast.

questions.q: In Close Ranks, what action does the 2nd rank take?
options: Stands fast
Takes 2 steps forward
Takes 1 step forward
Takes 1 step backward
questions.explanation: The 2nd rank takes 1 step forward in Close Ranks.

questions.q: In Close Ranks, how many steps does the 3rd rank take forward?
options: Takes 2 steps forward
Takes 1 step forward
Stands fast
Takes 3 steps forward
questions.explanation: The 3rd rank takes 2 steps forward in Close Ranks.

questions.q: In Close Ranks, how many steps does the 4th rank take forward?
options: 1 step forward
2 steps forward
Stands fast
3 steps forward
questions.explanation: The 4th rank takes 3 steps forward in Close Ranks.

questions.q: What is the step size for 'Right Step, MARCH'?
options: 6 inches
12 inches
18 inches
24 inches
questions.explanation: Right Step is executed in 12-inch lateral steps.

questions.q: From what movement state can 'Right Step, MARCH' be commanded?
options: Halt position only
While marching quick time
While marking time
During double time
questions.explanation: Right Step command is given only from a halt.

questions.q: When is 'Flight, HALT' commanded during Right Step?
options: Left foot strikes
Right foot strikes
Heels come together
Either toe touches
questions.explanation: To halt from Right Step, command 'Flight, HALT' as heels come together.

questions.q: What formation compiles a squadron into a compact block of multiple flights?
options: Column formation
Mass formation
Inverted line
Echelon formation
questions.explanation: A mass formation reduces width and increases depth for large ceremonies.

questions.q: How many paces in front of the squadron does the Squadron Commander stand?
options: 3 paces
6 paces
9 paces
12 paces
questions.explanation: Squadron commander positions 12 paces in front of squadron.

questions.q: In a squadron line of flights, how far in front stand Flight Commanders?
options: 6 paces
3 paces
12 paces
1 pace
questions.explanation: Flight commanders stand 6 paces in front of their respective flights in line.

questions.q: What is the standard minimum size of a military Color Guard team?
options: 2 members
3 members
4 members
6 members
questions.explanation: Color Guard consists of 4 members minimum (2 rifle bearers, 2 flag bearers).

questions.q: Where is the US National Flag carried relative to other flags in a Color Guard?
options: On the left
On the right
In the rear
In the exact center
questions.explanation: National Color is always positioned on the right of organizational colors.

questions.q: Under what condition does the US National Flag dip in salute during drill?
options: Never dips
Dips to the reviewing officer
Dips during national anthem
Dips to squadron commander
questions.explanation: The US Flag never dips to any person or object.

questions.q: Which flag dips during the playing of the National Anthem in ceremony?
options: US Flag
State Flag
City Flag
CAP Organizational Flag
questions.explanation: Organizational flags dip in salute when rendering honors.

questions.q: What command presents the flight in formal salute during ceremonies?
options: Parade Rest
Present, ARMS
Hand Salute
Order, ARMS
questions.explanation: 'Present, ARMS' renders a formal salute by formation.

questions.q: Which command terminates the position of Present Arms?
options: Ready, FRONT
At Ease
Order, ARMS
As You Were
questions.explanation: 'Order, ARMS' cancels Present Arms.

questions.q: What is a flight called if it faces opposite to its original front in line?
options: Inverted line
Inverted column
Reverse formation
Counter march
questions.explanation: An Inverted Line reverses front and rear facing of the formation.

questions.q: Which command reverses a column formation's direction in a narrow space?
options: To the Rear, MARCH
Counter, MARCH
Column Around, MARCH
About, MARCH
questions.explanation: 'Counter, MARCH' reverses marching direction of a column in limited space.

questions.q: In Counter March execution, how many steps does the lead element advance before turning?
options: 1 step
2 steps
4 steps
3 steps
questions.explanation: During Counter March, 1st element takes 3 steps past rear before turning.

questions.q: Who issues Supplementary Commands within a formation?
options: Element leaders
Reviewing officer
Guidon bearer
First sergeant only
questions.explanation: Supplementary commands are given by element leaders or sub-unit commanders.

questions.q: What type of command is 'PREPARE FOR INSPECTION'?
options: Combined command
Informational command
Supplementary command
Mass command
questions.explanation: Informational commands direct action without preparatory pauses.

questions.q: What class of command are 'FALL IN' and 'AT EASE'?
options: Supplementary
Directive
Informational
Combined command
questions.explanation: Combined commands combine preparatory and execution into one word.

questions.q: What is the space between individuals side by side called?
options: Distance
Depth
Interval
Alignment
questions.explanation: Interval is lateral distance between individuals side by side.

questions.q: What is the space between personnel from front to back called?
options: Distance
Interval
Width
Flank
questions.explanation: Distance is front-to-back space between ranks.

questions.q: What term describes dressing elements laterally on a straight line?
options: Covering
Alignment
Sizing
Pacing
questions.explanation: Alignment is dressing elements in a straight line.

questions.q: What term describes positioning directly behind the person in front of you?
options: Alignment
Dressing
Pacing
Covering
questions.explanation: Covering is aligning directly behind the person in front.

questions.q: What is the standard numerical size range of a single drill flight?
options: 8 to 30 cadets
2 to 5 cadets
40 to 60 cadets
100 cadets
questions.explanation: Flight size ranges from 8 to 30 cadets under normal standard.

questions.q: Which cadet regulates direction and cadence of the flight while marching?
options: Flight Sergeant
Element Leader
Flight Guide
Commander
questions.explanation: The Guide is responsible for maintaining direction and cadence.

questions.q: Where is the Guide positioned when marching in Column Formation?
options: Rear left
Front right of element 1
Center rank
Behind commander
questions.explanation: Guide position in column is in front of the right element.

questions.q: What command dismisses the Guidon Bearer individually?
options: GUIDON BEARER, DISMISSED
RETURN GUIDON
DROP GUIDON
GUIDON AT EASE
questions.explanation: 'GUIDON, BEARER, DISMISSED' dismisses the guidon.

questions.q: What is the standard marching position for holding the guidon staff?
options: Order Guidon
Present Guidon
Rest Guidon
Carry Guidon
questions.explanation: Carry Guidon is the standard position while marching.

questions.q: Where rests the base (ferrule) of the guidon staff at Order Guidon?
options: Raised 6 inches
Rests on ground by right toe
Held horizontal
Tucked under arm
questions.explanation: At Order Guidon, ferrule rests on the ground beside right shoe.

questions.q: What angle is the guidon staff held at Parade Rest?
options: Vertical
30 degrees
15 degrees forward
Horizontal
questions.explanation: Parade Rest with guidon tilts staff forward 15 degrees.

questions.q: How is Present Guidon executed during a salute?
options: Staff lowered horizontally forward
Staff held vertical overhead
Staff behind back
Staff touching left shoulder
questions.explanation: Present Guidon lowers staff horizontally forward.

questions.q: Which manual of arms command verifies a weapon is unloaded?
options: Present Arms
Inspection ARMS
Port ARMS
Order ARMS
questions.explanation: Inspection Arms is required before handling or inspecting weapons.

questions.q: Where is the rifle positioned during 'Port, ARMS'?
options: Vertical on right side
Horizontal at waist
Behind shoulder
Diagonally across chest 4 inches away
questions.explanation: Port Arms positions rifle diagonally across chest.

questions.q: Where is the rifle carried during 'Right Shoulder, ARMS'?
options: Right shoulder at 45 degrees
Left shoulder vertically
Under left arm
Across stomach
questions.explanation: Right Shoulder Arms rests rifle on right shoulder at 45 degrees.

questions.q: How is a flight sized when forming in line?

Tall on right, short on left
By rank order

SIZE THE FLIGHT
FALL IN BY RANK

Cadence count

Classroom lecture
Formal parade & pass in review
Radio net check

Honor, Courage, Commitment
Loyalty, Duty, Respect, Selfless Service
Leadership, Integrity, Service, Excellence

Curry Achievement

Chain of Command
Self-discipline

Punishing team members
Memorizing regulations

Warning and Execution
Primary and Secondary

Either foot
Both feet simultaneously
